local_checks.invariant: A recovery code is removed exactly once, even under concurrent use.
local_checks.result: Candidate: auth.ts:165-169 derives the remaining hash array from the challenge snapshot, and auth.ts:205 writes the whole array back. Two concurrent redemptions of different codes each overwrite the other, restoring one consumed code.

hardening_notes: verifyTotp explicitly documents that callers must reject a consumed step, so the missing conditional update is a contract gap rather than an unknown requirement.
Two concurrent /mfa/confirm calls can both return recovery codes while only one set is persisted, because the UPDATE is guarded by confirmed_at IS NULL but the response is not.

local_checks.invariant: Passwords are stored with a salted slow KDF and compared in constant time.
local_checks.result: Confirmed: PBKDF2-SHA256 with a per-hash random salt, 100,000 iterations (the Workers WebCrypto ceiling recorded in the project notes), and timingSafeCompare for digest comparison.

local_checks.invariant: TOTP secrets are sealed at rest and never fall back to plaintext in production.
local_checks.result: Confirmed: AES-256-GCM with user_mfa:<user id> as additional authenticated data; production without a valid 32-byte MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY returns 503 MFA_UNAVAILABLE instead of storing a plaintext secret.

local_checks.invariant: Security tokens have sufficient entropy and are stored hashed.
local_checks.result: Confirmed: 32 random bytes for session, reset, and activation tokens, stored as SHA-256 hashes; recovery codes are 8 symbols from a 32-symbol alphabet hashed with unsalted SHA-256.

hardening_notes: Recovery codes carry about 40 bits of entropy and are stored as unsalted SHA-256, so a database disclosure would allow offline enumeration; a keyed hash or longer code would raise the cost.
